answer: Each submission hangs on the sparrow of a task receipt, and the glacier is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Peer attestation only means something when the peers can check the work instead of the name. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short. The design leans on time-locked work history, clawed back after a replayed submission, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the ledge of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
